result.headline: Throttle command dropped to 0% at t=76 s and stayed there; altitude then fell.
result.explanation: A control fault occurred on the propulsion loop: throttle went 45 to 0% at 76.07 s and held to the end. ch[2] follows throttle, so the cut is upstream of the output. The recording does not show who or what commanded it.

evidence.quote: CONSTANT propulsion.throttle was varying, then held 0 from t=76.072 s to the end of the recording (15.995 s, 40 samples)
evidence.shows: Throttle was cut at 76.07 s and never recovered; no mode change or event explains it.

evidence.quote: CHANGE actuator.output[ch[2]] at t=76.207 s: 1464 -> 1100 us (step -364, 45.5x its usual variation)
evidence.shows: The propulsion channel dropped to its minimum 0.135 s after the throttle command; it is the follower.

evidence.quote: ROLE actuator.output[ch[2]] follows propulsion.throttle (correlation 0.994 over the recording): it serves that loop
evidence.shows: ch[2] is the propulsion loop output. Correlation was 0.992 at a 0.334 s lag over 60-92 s, so the output stage carried out the command.

evidence.quote: SHIFT vehicle.altitude[relative] changed level for good at t=82.65 s: median 49.642 before, 30.775 after m (20x its variation before)
evidence.shows: Altitude fell after the throttle cut, so this is a consequence of it.

evidence.quote: SHIFT vehicle.attitude[pitch] followed its setpoint worse for good from t=81.854 s: typical |error| 1.199 before, 6.296 after deg (6.6x its variation before)
evidence.shows: Pitch tracking degraded after the cut, as an effect of the descent.

checked.check: compare at t=76.072 (8 s window) to see what changed at the onset
checked.result: propulsion.throttle median 40.5 to 0 and flagged frozen. ch[2] 1428 to 1100 with spread 0. Roll, pitch and yaw tracking ratios stayed between 0.75 and 1.64, so no attitude loop froze.
correlation 0.992, best lag 0.334 s. The output stage follows the command, so the cut is upstream of ch[2].

checked.check: window 70-92 s on throttle, ch[2], altitude, pitch
checked.result: throttle was 45 at 74.903 s and 0 at 76.361 s. Altitude fell from 49.09 m at 76.816 s to 25.962 m at the end of the window. ch[1] fell to 1209 us as the pitch setpoint rose to 17.7 deg.
checked.about: Throttle cut is the earliest sign; the rest are effects

checked.check: sequence 55-92 s: who left baseline first
checked.result: The earliest departures are roll, yaw and velocity at 55 s (manoeuvre). The throttle cut at 76 s is not listed, so those changes cannot be separated from the manoeuvre. Median shifts in ch[2] and throttle earlier sit inside a varying manoeuvre.
The only events are start-up warnings at 0.677 s. No earlier case in the workspace.

outcomes.label: Failsafe or mode change at cut
outcomes.means: The throttle cut was commanded by the autopilot or an operator; propulsion hardware is not the fault.
outcomes.then: Trace the failsafe trigger, including low-voltage and sensor-health flags.

outcomes.label: Voltage or current collapse at cut
outcomes.means: A power-side cause. The low-voltage warning at start-up becomes relevant.
outcomes.then: Review pack condition and the battery log.

outcomes.label: No event and no power change
outcomes.means: The command source itself produced 0%; the cause is in the controller or its throttle input.
outcomes.then: Inspect the throttle source and RC link logs.

hypotheses.observed_at: controller output channel ch[2], not the ESC or motor itself

hypotheses.claim: A roll, pitch or yaw loop fault caused the failure.
hypotheses.because: Tracking ratios at 76 s were 0.75 to 1.64 and no attitude output froze. Pitch degradation came after the cut.

hypotheses.claim: A dead airspeed sensor or sensor-health fault led to the failsafe behaviour.
hypotheses.because: Airspeed is 0 for the whole recording and 'Sensor helth' errored at start-up, but nothing links either to 76 s.

events.what: Throttle cut 45 to 0% at 76.07 s, held; ch[2] to 1100 us
events.why: The only frozen output that follows an abrupt drop with no mode change.

events.what: Start-up battery low-voltage warning and sensor health error
events.why: They appear at 0.677 s and are not linked to 76 s by anything in the data.
The sensor may be absent or dead; it does not explain the cut.

events.what: Altitude loss, pitch tracking worse, ch[1] shift
events.why: These follow thrust loss after 76 s.

events.what: Roll, yaw and velocity manoeuvre steps
events.why: Manoeuvres that come back; attitude tracking stayed normal.

result.lesson: No earlier case in the workspace applies.
result.reuse_when: Fixed-wing or multirotor flights where the throttle command goes to 0 and holds with no mode or failsafe event, while the output channel still follows the command.
